entry.title: The Origin of the x86 ud2 Instruction Name
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | devblogs.microsoft.com | hacker news

The ud2 instruction is an architecturally undefined x86 instruction designed to trigger an "invalid opcode" exception. Compilers use it to mark unreachable code, ensuring that if execution flow erroneously reaches such a point, the program crashes immediately rather than executing unintended instructions.

The instruction's name is a result of the retroactive naming of previous, unofficial methods used to trigger the exception. Developers previously relied on the 0F FF and 0F B9 byte sequences to force invalid opcodes; as Intel formalized these behaviors, the 0F FF and 0F B9 sequences were designated ud0 and ud1, respectively, leaving ud2 as the standard, parameter-free instruction.
